site.name: Wolftone Mine
overview: The Wolftone was an important Carbonate Hill mine whose history extended beyond Leadville’s classic silver era into the later zinc economy.
It was connected historically with the broader A.M.W. operating context but remains a distinct mine from Maid of Erin, Adams, and neighboring properties.

timeline.text: The Wolftone developed as part of Leadville’s densely mined Carbonate Hill area.
EPA historical documentation records renewed operation after the mine was unwatered.
The property became important in Leadville’s shift toward zinc production.
Historical records document reprocessing of mine-dump material.
Waste from Wolftone and nearby mine areas was consolidated as part of California Gulch remediation work.

moreHistory: The Wolftone illustrates how one mine can pass through several industrial phases: underground production, changes in target commodities, dump reprocessing, and environmental remediation.
EPA records are especially useful for reconstructing both the operational history and later physical changes to the property.
USGS district studies provide the broader geological framework for the lead, silver, and zinc ores that shaped Carbonate Hill mining.
